title: Truncated nearby-cycle descent along a proper hypercover
statement: Let $S$ be Noetherian, $f:X\to S$ proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], $\Lambda$ finite killed by an integer invertible on $S$, and $K\in D^{\ge0}_c(X_{\mathrm{Et}},\Lambda)$ bounded above [def-weil-pbc-etale-constructible-sheaf]. Let $\epsilon:X_\bullet\to X$ be an augmented simplicial scheme whose degree-zero map and all matching maps $X_{n+1}\to(\operatorname{cosk}_n^X X_\bullet)_{n+1}$ are proper surjective. Here the matching scheme is the finite limit of the lower-degree face diagram; each $X_i$ is assumed finite type over $S$. Put $f_i=f\epsilon_i$ and $K_i=\epsilon_i^*K$. For every $r\ge-1$, if $P_{r-i}(f_i,K_i)$ holds for $0\le i\le r+1$, then $P_r(f,K)$ holds [def-trf-orgogozo-induction-data].

source.place: Lemmas 3.1.1--3.1.2, pp. 6--7, including the explicitly mentioned nonconstant-torsion-coefficient variant. Local archival PDF WANTED; author PDF read online.

proof.text: Fix an arbitrary preliminary base change $T\to S$ and an arbitrary further map $T'\to T$. Base change the given hypercover and $K$ to $T$. The proper-hypercover descent theorem supplies proper component augmentations and a proper hypercover after every further base change, including strict localizations and geometric fibres. The current definition of $P_s(g,L)$ requires $H^n\operatorname{Cone}(\beta)=0$ for $n\le s$ for every preliminary base change and every further base change, with the ordinary comparison of [def-trf-oriented-nearby-cycles]. Apply $P_{r-p}(f_p,K_p)$ with preliminary map $T\to S$ and further map $T'\to T$; its hypotheses require neither map to preserve Noetherianity. For a compatible geometric specialization $b'\to a'$ over $b\to a$ in $T'\to T$, use the sliced-comparison test to write $A=i_a^*Rj_{b,*}K_{(b)}$ on $X_{T,a}$ and $A'=i_{a'}^*Rj_{b',*}K_{T',(b')}$ on $X_{T',a'}$. It suffices to show $H^n\operatorname{Cone}(h^*A\to A')=0$ for $n\le r$, for every such choice.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.1, first proof paragraph; universal version by applying the argument after every T -> S.

proof.text:
Write $\epsilon_{(a)},\epsilon_{(b)},\epsilon_a$ for the augmentations over $T_{(a)},T_{(b)},a$ and $j_\bullet,i_\bullet$ for the levelwise maps. Descent on $X_{T,(b)}$ gives $K_{(b)}\simeq R\epsilon_{(b),*}K_{\bullet,(b)}$. The equality $j_b\epsilon_{(b)}=\epsilon_{(a)}j_\bullet$ and the canonical derived composition isomorphisms give
$$A\simeq i_a^*R\epsilon_{(a),*}Rj_{\bullet,*}K_{\bullet,(b)}\simeq R\epsilon_{a,*}(i_\bullet^*Rj_{\bullet,*}K_{\bullet,(b)}).$$
The last isomorphism is simplicial proper exchange for the Cartesian square over $i_a$. Set $A_\bullet=i_\bullet^*Rj_{\bullet,*}K_{\bullet,(b)}$. Its component in degree $p$ is $i_{p,a}^*Rj_{p,b,*}K_{p,(b)}$, by componentwise derived restriction. Apply exactly these constructions to $T'$ to obtain $A'\simeq R\epsilon_{a',*}A'_\bullet$. These are statements about complexes on the simplicial total topos, not merely a collection of unrelated component isomorphisms.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.1, cohomological descent and first displayed canonical isomorphism; Stacks 0DHL, 0DH1, 0D7F.

proof.text: Let $h:X_{T',a'}\to X_{T,a}$ and $h_\bullet:X_{\bullet,T',a'}\to X_{\bullet,T,a}$ be the fibre maps. Simplicial proper exchange gives $h^*R\epsilon_{a,*}A_\bullet\simeq R\epsilon_{a',*}h_\bullet^*A_\bullet$. Under this isomorphism and Step 2, the sliced comparison $h^*A\to A'$ equals $R\epsilon_{a',*}(\delta_\bullet)$, where $\delta_\bullet:h_\bullet^*A_\bullet\to A'_\bullet$ has the ordinary sliced comparisons in each degree. To check the map, use the descent units in Step 2 and the counit-defined exchanges: the augmentation pullbacks send a coefficient section to its pullback, the comparison evaluates the pulled-back direct-image section, and both routes then restrict it along $T'\to T$. Naturality of the descent unit and the unit/counit compatibility of the derived composition and exchange maps identify these two composites before derivation. Their canonical derived maps therefore agree. In particular this is the ordinary $\beta$ comparison tested by the slice lemma.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.1, commutative square and the proper-exchange isomorphism at its upper right.

proof.text: Form $D_\bullet=\operatorname{Cone}(\delta_\bullet)$ in the derived category of the simplicial total topos. Exactness of $R\epsilon_{a',*}$ identifies the cone of the comparison of Step 3 with $R\epsilon_{a',*}D_\bullet$. Exact component restriction identifies $D_p$ with the cone of the degree-$p$ sliced comparison. Both source and target of $\delta_\bullet$ have cohomology in degrees $\ge0$: inverse images are exact, and a right derived direct image is computed on an injective representative zero below $0$. These categories have enough injectives: on any of the small sites a termwise-injective resolution $F[0]\to I$ gives a monomorphism $F\to I^0$, since its map on $H^0$ is an isomorphism. The total site is small in the chosen universe (a countable union of its component sites), so the general module-resolution theorem applies there too. The bounded-below representative theorem can therefore be applied with lower bound $0$. The cone long exact sequence then gives $H^q(D_\bullet)=0$ for $q<-1$; it does not give vanishing in degree $-1$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.1, final sentence, and Lemma 3.1.2, lower bound -1; Stacks derived.tex Tag 05TC (lemma-negative-vanishing).

proof.text: For $0\le p\le r+1$, apply the two quantifiers in $P_{r-p}(f_p,K_p)$ to the fixed maps $T\to S$ and $T'\to T$. The cone of this degree-$p$ ordinary comparison has $H^q=0$ for $q\le r-p$, with the inclusive bound in the current definition. The sliced-comparison test identifies its restriction with $D_p$, giving the same vanishing for $D_p$. Thus $D_p$ has an injective representative zero below $r-p+1$. Applying the component direct image to that representative shows $H^q(R\epsilon_{p,a',*}D_p)=0$ for $q\le r-p$. For every $p$, including those beyond $r+1$, the same reasoning applied to the uniform lower bound $-1$ in Step 4 shows $H^q(R\epsilon_{p,a',*}D_p)=0$ for $q<-1$. This only uses a lower bound, so the images of the nearby complexes need not be bounded above.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2, proof, derived direct image preserves the lower vanishing bound; explicit injective argument for its final sentence.

proof.text:
Apply the augmentation spectral sequence to $D_\bullet$ with uniform bound $c=-1$:
$$E_1^{p,q}=H^q(R\epsilon_{p,a',*}D_p)\Longrightarrow H^{p+q}(R\epsilon_{a',*}D_\bullet),\quad p\ge0,\ q\ge-1.$$
Fix $n\le r$. If $n<-1$ there are no terms of total degree $n$. Otherwise every possible term has $0\le p\le n+1\le r+1$ and $q=n-p\le r-p$, so Step 5 kills it. A zero page term remains zero on every subsequent page, since the next term is a quotient of a subobject of it. Hence every associated graded object of the abutment in degree $n$ is zero. The filtration has only $n+2$ possible nonzero graded positions ($0\le p\le n+1$), so induction from its zero last step gives $H^n(R\epsilon_{a',*}D_\bullet)=0$. At $r=-1$ the only possible boundary term is $(p,q)=(0,-1)$, killed by $P_{-1}(f_0,K_0)$.

source.place: Lemma 3.1.2, augmentation spectral sequence and finite-diagonal vanishing argument; Stacks 0D7F.

proof.text: Steps 3--6 show the required vanishing of every sliced comparison cone for $f_T$ and $T'\to T$. The sliced-comparison test gives vanishing in degrees $\le r$ of the ordinary comparison cone on the whole vanishing topos. Since both $T\to S$ and $T'\to T$ were arbitrary, the ordinary comparison cone vanishes in every degree $n\le r$ after every such pair. This is precisely the current two-quantifier definition of $P_r(f,K)$; no modification, alteration or semistable-tower clause of that definition node is used.
